meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's essay, and the zero you entered without calling me.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. On what basis was there a zero at all?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
Put a seventeen-year-old on the spot about his own essay and he'll fumble. And "like, being stuck" isn't wrong. Show me the note you wrote that day.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their thesis between an outline and an essay; that's what drafting is for. Put the outline and the essay in front of me. And I'm still waiting on that note.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Nothing on his record, the mark replaced, in writing: that's your own procedure, and I'll hold you to it. But a rewrite on the strength of things you've described and not shown me is Owen admitting to something. The note and the outline, on this desk, before I agree to anything.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. Before I agree to that rewrite, I want copies of the note you wrote on November 2 and the October 15 outline, alongside the essay. You said you would send me the offer in writing by Friday at 3 PM, and I expect it by then.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she accepted your written commitment that nothing goes on his record and the new mark replaces the zero, but she still wants to see the November 2 note and the October 15 outline before she agrees to the rewrite. The fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you were one step away; her time had not run out.
What moved her: you committed to procedure 4.4 in writing, which met the one thing she would never give up.
What cost ground: you offered the rewrite before you showed her any document, so accepting it would have felt like Owen admitting something.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence was about the October 15 outline and your November 2 conversation, so it never came near that night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked to see the note you wrote on November 2, put it on the desk with the outline and the essay side by side before you make your offer.
